claim: Commercial dual-rail instant payments (RTP $10M, FedNow $1M); FedNow limit $1M (other_flags.fednow_limit).
finding: The Federal Reserve raised the FedNow per-transaction network limit from $1M to $10M effective November 2025. U.S. Bank's own Instant Payments API v2 page (rendered in browser) states a $10M limit for both TCH RTP and FedNow. The commercial RTP/FedNow marketing page (modified 2026-06-05) still says FedNow $1M — a stale bank page, not the current limit.
resolution: RTP and FedNow: $10M per transaction (U.S. Bank Instant Payments API; FedNow network limit since Nov 2025). U.S. Bank's commercial marketing page still shows FedNow $1M (stale).

claim: The 2023 FedNow fact sheet cited $1M for FedNow (and RTP $10M).
finding: In July 2023 the RTP limit was $1M and FedNow launched with a $500K maximum; the fact sheet lists '$1 million' and '$500,000' under 'The transaction limit' (layout ambiguous). The researcher's reading (FedNow $1M / RTP $10M in 2023) does not match either the PDF or the 2023 network limits. RTP went to $10M in Feb 2025; FedNow to $1M mid-2025 and $10M Nov 2025.
resolution: July 2023 fact sheet lists $1M and $500K without network labels; these match the then-current RTP $1M / FedNow $500K limits. Current limits are $10M for both. Open question resolved.

claim: Chapter's consumer inventory and 2025–2026 changes do not mention Payment Switch.
finding: U.S. Bank launched Payment Switch on Oct 19 2026: customers move recurring bills and subscriptions to a U.S. Bank debit or credit card from the Bills & Subscriptions dashboard in the mobile app, powered by Atomic (which also powers automated direct-deposit set-up; part of the 'Easy Switch' solution). The chapter's Oct 2026 release-note item ('streamlined direct-deposit enrollment') is the same Atomic programme but Payment Switch itself is missing.
resolution: Add sub-product 'Payment Switch' under USB-P05 (rail OTHER; vendor Atomic) and a recent change dated Oct 19 2026.

claim: Bill pay for business vendor 'Not named (third-party AP platform embedded; vendor not disclosed)'.
finding: U.S. Bank's own Aug 29 2025 Business Wire release (S117, previously only summary_only) states that bill pay for business is powered by Fiserv's CashFlow Central, built with Melio.

claim: Payee Choice former name: 'Supplier Prefer Pay (2017 supplier-enrollment product, S068)'.
finding: The 2017 release announced two separate products: Disbursements via Zelle (B2C) and Supplier Prefer Pay, a B2B supplier-enablement service moving suppliers from checks to virtual card and ACH. Payee Choice is a B2C payee-choice disbursement platform (RTP, Zelle, push-to-card, ACH, prepaid, check). Nothing links the two names.
resolution: Remove from Payee Choice former_names; note Supplier Prefer Pay as a historic B2B AP product.

claim: Commercial money-movement inventory is complete (SinglePoint, instant payments, Payee Choice, Zelle disbursements, push-to-card, Pay Smart, international).
finding: The commercial Accounts payable hub also markets U.S. Bank AP Optimizer® (invoice-to-pay automation), virtual credit cards, U.S. Bank prepaid solutions (B2C disbursement), check processing, and virtual account management. Card-based B2B payables and prepaid disbursements are money-movement products the chapter does not inventory.
resolution: Record as coverage gap: add a coverage note listing AP Optimizer®, virtual credit cards and U.S. Bank prepaid disbursements (commercial, rail OTHER) without journey mapping.

claim: SMB inventory does not include U.S. Bank invoicing.
finding: The Nov 2 2026 'Tour of business online banking' (S917, already in sources) promotes U.S. Bank invoicing: send branded invoices and receive payments by card or bank account; Digital Explorer lists a dedicated 'U.S. Bank invoicing' demo (/content/275). It appears in data only as a recent-changes mention, not as a product.
resolution: Add to coverage_self_assessment.known_gaps_in_evidence and open questions: 'U.S. Bank invoicing (SMB, card/bank-account collection) exists (S917) – rails and flow not mapped.'

claim: '...no foreign-currency or remittance product exists for consumers.'
finding: Digital Explorer's Transfer and pay channel includes 'Order foreign currency with the mobile app' (consumer foreign-cash ordering). It is not a remittance, so the remittance half of the claim stands; the foreign-currency half is wrong.
resolution: 'Consumers cannot send international wires digitally (branch or phone only) and have no remittance/cross-border transfer product; the only consumer FX capability is ordering foreign cash in the mobile app (S005, S050, S956).'

claim: Digital wires visible only to customers with ≥6 months history and an 'eligible direct-deposit account'.
finding: KB0209664 requires a checking, savings or money market account (a deposit account), ≥6 months as a customer and a registered cellular device; no direct-deposit requirement is stated.
resolution: 'eligible checking, savings or money market account (registered cellular device ≥3 business days)'.

claim: Action: 'Check the box acknowledging the payment can't be cancelled...; review details; select Send'.
finding: The live demo order is: 'Review before sending.' screen > 'Send $X' > full-screen 'Keep your money safe.' warning with checkbox 'I understand that once my payment is sent, it can't be canceled.' > Continue. The checkbox comes after Send, not before. The patched system_behavior field says this correctly but the action text was not updated.
resolution: Action rewritten to reflect Review > Send $X > 'Keep your money safe.' checkbox > Continue.

claim: Step numbers are sequential within each journey.
finding: The gap-fill patch broke numbering: J01 REVIEW_AUTHORIZE is numbered 1,2,3 between INITIATE 6 and EXECUTE_TRACK 9; J07 REVIEW_AUTHORIZE is 1,2 between INITIATE 4 and EXECUTE_TRACK 6; J09 SET_UP is 1,2 after DISCOVER 1. This is a data-integrity defect that will mis-sort steps in the consolidated deck.
resolution: Renumber sequentially as specified in the correction patch.

target: USB-J01 exception 'Authorized push payment scam (imposter)'; USB-J01/EXCEPTION/15
claim: Scam victims call the Fraud Liaison Center (877-595-6256).
finding: U.S. Bank pages differ: the Zelle for business page and Zelle support page direct scam/dispute contacts to 800-USBANKS (872-2657); the digital-payments-scam education page names the Fraud Liaison Center. Both are valid entry points; the chapter names only one.
resolution: 'Call 800-USBANKS (Zelle pages) or the Fraud Liaison Center 877-595-6256 (scam guidance page); no in-app scam-claim path.'

claim: Smart Assistant initiates bill payments (rail BILL_PAY).
finding: The Smart Assistant page gives 'Pay the statement balance on my credit card', 'Send 200 bucks to Tony' and 'Transfer $100 from savings to checking'. It does not name bill pay or Zelle. Paying a U.S. Bank card is an internal payment, not third-party bill pay.
resolution: USB-P07 rails: INTERNAL_TRANSFER, ZELLE (INFERRED), OTHER; sub-product description: 'P2P send (Zelle INFERRED), internal transfers and U.S. Bank credit-card payments; third-party bill pay via assistant not documented'.

claim: Oct 27 2026 Google Play release includes mobile deposit 'now with increased limits'.
finding: The Oct 27 2026 'What's new' text lists only direct-deposit enrollment, home value in net worth and transaction search. 'Quickly deposit checks, now with increased limits.' is in the undated 'About this app' description.

claim: Standard outbound external transfer available in 1–3 business days.
finding: Bank pages conflict: the Transfer money page and KB0070109 say 1–3 business days, while KB0250043 says outbound funds are typically available two to three business days after initiation.
resolution: Keep '1–3 business days (KB0250043 says 2–3)'; add an open question.

finding: U.S. Bank's own Zelle landing page confirms the service in its app and online banking, so the evidence level should be CONFIRMED_BANK (the zelle.com list corroborates).

target: rail_participation.fednow_send / push_to_card vs the participation baseline participation
finding: Challenge raised because the participation baseline → participation['us-bank'] shows fednow_send 'unknown' and push_to_card 'unknown'. Re-check: U.S. Bank's Instant Payments API lets clients send credit transfers via FedNow, and the Push to Card API sends to Visa/Mastercard debit cards. The bank chapter is right and the cross-bank matrix is stale.
resolution: No the research dataset change. Recommend the participation baseline fednow_send=true, push_to_card=true (commercial).

claim: International wire digital for business accounts only; consumers branch/phone; business digital fee $45 ($35 with Enhanced Payments); same-day only 7:30–3 CT; USD only.
finding: Tested whether consumers can now send international wires digitally (the July 2026 Enhanced Payments release made business international wires digital). KB0069815 still marks the digital route 'Business deposit accounts only'; the $45/$35 fees come from the Enhanced Payments comparison table; the cut-off and no-future-dating rules appear in the KB.
